ee:2026:q1.question:
Consider the infinite-length, discrete-time sequence $x[n] = 0.9^{|n|}$, where $n$ is an integer.

The region of convergence of its Z-transform $X(z)$ is given by:
(Note: $z$ is a complex variable)

detailed_solution.markdown: Split $x[n] = 0.9^{|n|}$ into two parts: Causal part: $0.9^{n}u[n]$ ROC: $|z| > 0.9$ Anti-causal part: $0.9^{-n}u[-n-1]$ ROC: $|z| < \frac{1}{0.9}$ ROC of bilateral Z-transform = intersection: $0.9 < |z| < \dfrac{1}{0.9}$ Answer: (C) Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ee:2026:q2.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 2
ee:2026:q2.question:
Let $x_c(t)$ be any continuous-time periodic signal with period $T$. It is sampled uniformly with a sampling period $T_s$ where $T_s \neq T$, resulting in the discrete sequence

$x[n] = x_c(nT_s)$, where $n$ is an integer.

Which one of the following statements is correct about $x[n]$?
options: $x[n]$ will always be periodic with period $T/T_s$ for all values of $T/T_s$
$x[n]$ will always be periodic with period $1$ for all values of $T/T_s$
$x[n]$ will be periodic if and only if $T/T_s$ is a rational number

detailed_solution.markdown: For $x[n] = x_c(nT_s)$ to be periodic with integer period $N$: $x_c(nT_s) = x_c((n+N)T_s)$ This requires $NT_s = kT$ for some integer $k$. $\Rightarrow \dfrac{T}{T_s} = \dfrac{N}{k} \in \mathbb{Q}$ (rational) $x[n]$ is periodic if and only if $T/T_s$ is rational. Answer: (D) Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ee:2026:q3.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 3
ee:2026:q3.question:
The Laplace transform of the step response of a system is given by

$Y(s) = \dfrac{100}{s(s + 100)}$

The rise time is defined as the time taken for the response to go from 0.1 to 0.9 of its final value. The settling time is defined as the time taken for the response to reach 0.98 of its final value.

For this system, the rise time $(T_r)$, settling time $(T_s)$, and time constant $(T_c)$, all expressed in seconds, are

detailed_solution.markdown: Step response: $y(t) = 1 - e^{-100t}$ Time constant: $T_c = 1/100 = 0.01$ s Rise time (0.1 to 0.9): $t_1 = -\ln(0.9)/100 \approx 0.00105$ s $t_2 = -\ln(0.1)/100 \approx 0.02303$ s $T_r = t_2 - t_1 \approx 0.022$ s Settling time (to 0.98): $0.98 = 1 - e^{-100T_s} \Rightarrow T_s = -\ln(0.02)/100 \approx 0.04s$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2026:q6.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 6
ee:2026:q6.question:
A positive point charge with velocity $\vec{v} = 5\hat{x}$ enters a region having electric field $\vec{E} = 4\hat{y}$ and magnetic field $\vec{B} = -6\hat{z}$.

Which one of the following statements is correct for the force on the charge as it enters the region?
options: The force will be along the magnetic field but perpendicular to the electric field
The force will be along the electric field but perpendicular to the magnetic field
The force will be perpendicular to both electric and magnetic field
The magnetic field does not exert any force on the charge

detailed_solution.markdown: Lorentz force: $\vec{F} = q(\vec{E} + \vec{v} \times \vec{B})$ Electric force: $q \cdot 4\hat{y}$ -> along $\hat{y}$ Magnetic force: $\vec{v} \times \vec{B} = 5\hat{x} \times (-6\hat{z}) = -30(\hat{x} \times \hat{z}) = -30(-\hat{y}) = 30\hat{y}$ Total force: $\vec{F} = q(4 + 30)\hat{y} = 34q\hat{y}$ Force is along $\hat{y}$ = along $\vec{E}$, and $\hat{y} \perp \hat{z}$ (perpendicular to $\vec{B}$). Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ee:2026:q7.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 7
ee:2026:q7.question:
A 15 kVA, 1100 V/220 V, single-phase two-winding transformer is configured as a 1.32 kV/1.1 kV autotransformer.

What will be the rating of the autotransformer?

detailed_solution.markdown:
For an autotransformer formed from a two-winding transformer:

$S_{auto} = S_{tw} \times \dfrac{V_H}{V_H - V_L}$

Here $V_H = 1320$ V, $V_L = 1100$ V (series winding = 220 V):

$S_{auto} = 15 \times \dfrac{1320}{1320 - 1100} = 15 \times \dfrac{1320}{220} = 15 \times 6 = 90$ kVA

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ee:2026:q8.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 8
ee:2026:q8.question:
Consider a power system with $N$ buses, of which $P$ are generator buses and the remaining $Q$ are load buses (where there is no generation).

Assume that there are no reactive power-limit violations at the generator buses.

What is the size of the Jacobian matrix in the Newton-Raphson load flow method?

detailed_solution.markdown: Given: A power system has $N$ buses, of which: $P$ are generator buses (including the slack bus) $Q$ are load (PQ) buses Hence, $N=P+Q$ Step 1: Count the unknown voltage angles In the Newton-Raphson load flow method, the voltage angle of the slack bus is known. Therefore, voltage angles of all remaining buses are unknown. $\text{Number of angle unknowns}=N-1$ Step 2: Count the unknown voltage magnitudes Voltage magnitudes are known at generator (PV) buses and at the slack bus. They are unknown only at PQ buses. Therefore, $\text{Number of magnitude unknowns}=Q$ Step 3: Total number of unknowns $(N-1)+Q$ Using $Q=N-P$, $(N-1)+(N-P) = 2N-1-P$ Step 4: Size of the Jacobian matrix The Jacobian matrix is a square matrix whose order equals the total number of unknown variables. Hence, $\text{Jacobian Size} = (2N-1-P)\times(2N-1-P)$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ee:2026:q9.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 9
ee:2026:q9.question:
The initial three-phase voltage phasors $(\bar{V}_A,\ \bar{V}_B,\ \bar{V}_C)$ at a bus of a power network are as shown in Case-1. Due to a disturbance, the bus voltage phasors changed in phase by a small angle $\Delta\theta$, and the magnitudes remained the same as depicted in Case-2.



Which one of the following statements is correct about the zero sequence components?
options: The zero sequence components in Case-1 and Case-2 have the same phase angle and magnitude
The magnitude of the zero sequence component in Case-1 is greater than that in Case-2
The magnitude of the zero sequence component in Case-2 is greater than that in Case-1
The zero sequence components in Case-1 and Case-2 have the same magnitude but different phase angles

detailed_solution.markdown: Concept: The zero-sequence component of a three-phase set is $V_0=\frac{V_A+V_B+V_C}{3}$ Case-1: The phase voltages are $V_A=V_A\angle\theta_A,\qquad V_B=V_B\angle\theta_B,\qquad V_C=V_C\angle\theta_C$ Therefore, $V_{0,1} = \frac{V_A\angle\theta_A+V_B\angle\theta_B+V_C\angle\theta_C}{3}$ Case-2: Each phasor is rotated by the same angle $\Delta\theta$, while its magnitude remains unchanged. Hence, $V_A'=V_A\angle(\theta_A+\Delta\theta)$ $V_B'=V_B\angle(\theta_B+\Delta\theta)$ $V_C'=V_C\angle(\theta_C+\Delta\theta)$ The new zero-sequence component is $V_{0,2} = \frac{V_A'+V_B'+V_C'}{3}$ Substituting, $V_{0,2} = \frac{ V_A\angle(\theta_A+\Delta\theta) + V_B\angle(\theta_B+\Delta\theta) + V_C\angle(\theta_C+\Delta\theta) }{3}$ Factoring out $e^{j\Delta\theta}$, $V_{0,2} = e^{j\Delta\theta} \frac{ V_A\angle\theta_A + V_B\angle\theta_B + V_C\angle\theta_C }{3}$ $V_{0,2} = e^{j\Delta\theta}V_{0,1}$ Observation: Multiplication by $e^{j\Delta\theta}$ rotates a phasor by $\Delta\theta$ but does not change its magnitude. Therefore, $|V_{0,2}|=|V_{0,1}|$ and $\angle V_{0,2} = \angle V_{0,1} + \Delta\theta$ Hence, the zero-sequence components in the two cases have the same magnitude but different phase angles. Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ee:2026:q10.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 10
ee:2026:q10.question:
A certain application requires power at a frequency of 16.67 Hz, while the available grid frequency is 50 Hz. A 3-phase synchronous motor connected to the 50 Hz, 3-phase grid, driving a synchronous generator, is used for this application.

ee:2026:q11.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 11
ee:2026:q11.question: Which one of the following options is correct regarding the typical double-squirrel-cage structure used in induction motors?
options: At starting, a larger portion of the rotor current flows in the outer cage
At starting, a larger portion of the rotor current flows in the inner cage
At rated speed, most of the rotor current flows in the outer cage
The purpose of the double-squirrel-cage structure is to lower the effective rotor resistance at starting

detailed_solution.concept: Electrical Machines - Three Phase Induction Machines
detailed_solution.markdown: Concept of Double-Squirrel-Cage Induction Motor A double-squirrel-cage rotor consists of two cages: 1. Outer cage - High resistance - Low reactance 2. Inner cage - Low resistance - High reactance At starting: The slip is $s=1$. Therefore, rotor frequency is maximum, and rotor reactance becomes significant. Since the inner cage has high reactance, its impedance is large: $Z_{\text{inner}} = R_{\text{inner}} + jX_{\text{inner}}$ with $X_{\text{inner}} \gg X_{\text{outer}}$ Hence, most of the rotor current flows through the outer cage, which has lower impedance. The high resistance of the outer cage provides a high starting torque. At rated speed: The slip is very small. Hence rotor frequency is low and rotor reactance becomes negligible. Current distribution is then determined mainly by resistance. Since $R_{\text{inner}} < R_{\text{outer}}$ most of the rotor current flows through the inner cage. Thus the motor behaves like a low-resistance rotor during normal operation, giving good efficiency. The purpose is actually to obtain high effective rotor resistance at starting and low effective rotor resistance during normal running. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2026:q12.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 12
ee:2026:q12.question:
The figure shows the single-line diagram of a synchronous generator delivering $P = 50$ MW of power at unity power factor to an infinite bus.



$I_s$ denotes the stator current phasor. If the field excitation is increased, which one of the following options correctly describes its effect on the stator current, power factor, and load angle of the machine?
options: Stator current increases, power factor becomes lagging, load angle remains the same
Stator current decreases, power factor becomes leading, load angle remains the same
Stator current increases, power factor becomes lagging, load angle decreases
Stator current increases, power factor becomes leading, load angle increases

detailed_solution.markdown: Concept: A synchronous generator connected to an infinite bus operates with: $P=\frac{EV}{X_s}\sin\delta$ where $E$ = internal generated emf, $V$ = infinite-bus voltage, $X_s$ = synchronous reactance, $\delta$ = load angle. Step 1: What happens when field excitation is increased? Increasing field current increases the internal emf $E$ of the generator. Step 2: Real power remains unchanged The mechanical input power is unchanged, and the generator is delivering $P=50\ \text{MW}$ to an infinite bus. Hence, $P=\dfrac{EV}{X_s}\sin\delta$ must remain constant. Since $E$ increases, the quantity $\sin\delta$ must decrease. Therefore, $\delta$ decreases. Step 3: Effect on reactive power and power factor Initially, the generator operates at unity power factor. When excitation is increased, the generator becomes over-excited and supplies reactive power to the system. Thus the stator current leads the terminal voltage. Hence the power factor becomes leading. Step 4: Effect on stator current magnitude Initially, $I_s$ is in phase with $V$ (unity power factor). After over-excitation: Real power component of current remains essentially unchanged. A leading reactive current component appears. Therefore, $|I_s| = \sqrt{I_P^2+I_Q^2}$ increases. So the stator current magnitude increases. Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ee:2026:q15.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 15
ee:2026:q15.question:
Refer to the four circuits shown:



Which one of the following options for $k_1, k_2, k_3$, and $k_4$ makes all of them realizable?
options: $k_1 = 1,\ k_4 = -1/3$, for all values of $k_2$ and $k_3$
$k_2 = -2,\ k_3 = +1/3$, for all values of $k_1$ and $k_4$

primary.subtopicLabel: Two Port Network and Network Functions

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Two Port Network and Network Functions
detailed_solution.markdown: Concept: A dependent source is realizable only if it does not violate KVL or KCL. For an ideal loop of voltage sources, KVL must be satisfied. For an ideal cut-set of current sources, KCL must be satisfied. We examine each circuit separately. Circuit-1: Voltage source controlling a voltage source The two voltage sources are connected in parallel. Hence, $V_X=V_D$ But, $V_X=k_1V_D$ Therefore, $k_1V_D=V_D$ For any value of $V_D$, $\boxed{k_1=1}$ Circuit-2: Voltage source controlling a current source An ideal voltage source is connected in parallel with an ideal current source. There is no contradiction. The voltage source fixes the voltage, while the current source fixes the current. Hence, $\boxed{k_2\text{ can have any value}}$ Circuit-3: Current source controlling a voltage source An ideal current source is connected in parallel with an ideal voltage source. Again, there is no contradiction. The current source fixes the current, while the voltage source fixes the voltage. Hence, $\boxed{k_3\text{ can have any value}}$ Circuit-4: Current source controlling a current source The two current sources are connected in parallel. Applying KCL, $I_D+I_X=0$ Given, $I_X=3k_4I_D$ Substituting, $I_D+3k_4I_DI=0$ $(1+3k_4)I_D=0$ For all values of $I_D$, $1+3k_4=0$ $\boxed{k_4=-\frac13}$ Comparing with the options: Only Option (A) satisfies $k_1=1, k_4=-\frac13$ while $k_2$ and $k_3$ can be arbitrary. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2026:q16.question:

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Steady state AC Analysis
detailed_solution.markdown: Voltage is purely at 50 Hz -> only the 50 Hz current component contributes to real power. ee:2026:q19.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 19
ee:2026:q19.question:
The asymptotic Bode magnitude plot of a system is shown.



Which one of the following options best represents the transfer function of the system?

detailed_solution.markdown: Concept: The slope of the asymptotic Bode magnitude plot helps identify the poles and zeros of the transfer function. Step 1: Observe the low-frequency behavior The magnitude plot has a slope of $-20\ \text{dB/decade}$ for frequencies below $\omega_0.$ A slope of $-20\ \text{dB/decade}$ indicates the presence of a pole at the origin. Thus, the transfer function contains the factor $\frac{1}{s/\omega_0}.$ Step 2: Observe the break frequency At $\omega=\omega_0,$ the slope changes from $-20\ \text{dB/decade} \] to [latex] 0\ \text{dB/decade}.$ A change in slope of $+20\ \text{dB/decade}$ indicates the presence of a zero at $\omega=\omega_0.$ Hence, the transfer function also contains the factor $1+\frac{s}{\omega_0}.$ Step 3: Form the transfer function Combining the pole at the origin and the zero at $\omega_0,$ we obtain $G(s) = \frac{1+\dfrac{s}{\omega_0}} {\dfrac{s}{\omega_0}}.$ Verification: For $\omega \ll \omega_0,$ $G(j\omega)\approx\frac{1}{j\omega/\omega_0},$ which gives a slope of $-20\ \text{dB/decade}.$ For $\omega \gg \omega_0,$ $G(j\omega)\approx \frac{j\omega/\omega_0}{j\omega/\omega_0}=1,$ so the magnitude becomes $0\ \text{dB},$ which matches the given Bode plot. Therefore, the correct transfer function is $\boxed{G(s)=\frac{1+\dfrac{s}{\omega_0}}{\dfrac{s}{\omega_0}}}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2026:q21.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 21
ee:2026:q21.question:
A 220V/12V single-phase transformer is designed for use in India and rated 100 VA at 50 Hz. Later, this unit is shipped to the USA where it is used as a 110V/6V transformer at 60 Hz.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: No-load current drawn would be smaller for operation in the USA compared to that in India
For the same load current, the losses would be higher in the USA compared to that in India
The peak magnetic flux density in the core would be higher while operating in the USA compared to that in India
The eddy current losses in the core would be approximately 44% higher while operating in the USA compared to that in India

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given: Transformer rating:
  • India: $220/12\text{ V},\ 50\text{ Hz},\ 100\text{ VA}$
  • USA: $110/6\text{ V},\ 60\text{ Hz}$
Since both the primary and secondary voltages are reduced by half, the turns ratio remains unchanged. Step 1: Compare the peak flux density The maximum flux in a transformer is given by $E=4.44fN\phi_{\max}$ Hence, $\phi_{\max}\propto\frac{V}{f}$ For India, $\frac{V}{f} = \frac{220}{50} = 4.4$ For the USA, $\frac{V}{f} = \frac{110}{60} = 1.833$ Thus, $\phi_{\max,\text{USA}} < \phi_{\max,\text{India}}$ Therefore, the peak magnetic flux density is lower in the USA. Hence, (C) is incorrect. Step 2: No-load current The no-load current mainly consists of the magnetizing current, which is proportional to the core flux. Since the flux is lower in the USA, $I_{0,\text{USA}} < I_{0,\text{India}}$ Therefore, (A) is correct. Step 3: Copper losses Copper loss is $P_{cu}=I^2R.$ The statement specifies the same load current. Since the winding resistance remains unchanged, $P_{cu,\text{USA}} = P_{cu,\text{India}}.$ Thus, the losses are not higher in the USA. Hence, (B) is incorrect. Step 4: Eddy current loss Eddy current loss is proportional to $P_e\propto B_{\max}^2f^2.$ Since $B_{\max}\propto\frac{V}{f},$ $P_e \propto \left(\frac{V}{f}\right)^2f^2 = V^2.$ Therefore, $\frac{P_{e,\text{USA}}}{P_{e,\text{India}}} = \left(\frac{110}{220}\right)^2 = \frac14.$ Thus, $P_{e,\text{USA}} = 25\% \text{ of } P_{e,\text{India}}.$ The eddy current loss is approximately 75% lower, not 44% higher. Hence, (D) is incorrect. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2026:q22.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 22

A time-limited waveform $g(x)$ is specified as follows:

$$g(x) = \begin{cases} -k, & -\pi < x \leq 0 \\ +k, & 0 < x \leq \pi \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

A new waveform $f(x)$ is constructed from $g(x)$ as follows:
$$f(x) = \displaystyle\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty} g(x + 2\pi m)$$, for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$

The sum of the coefficients of the third harmonics of the sine and cosine terms in the trigonometric Fourier series expansion of $f(x)$ is $\dfrac{2}{3\pi}$.

detailed_solution.markdown:
A periodic function is formed as $f(x)=\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty}g(x+2\pi m),$ which is a periodic function with period $2\pi.$ Step 1: Identify the symmetry Since $f(-x)=-f(x),$ the function is odd. Hence,
  • All cosine coefficients are zero.
  • Only sine coefficients are present.
Therefore, $a_n=0.$ Step 2: Calculate the sine coefficients The sine coefficient is $b_n=\dfrac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)\sin(nx)\,dx.$ Substituting the given waveform, $b_n = \dfrac{1}{\pi} \left[ \int_{-\pi}^{0}(-k)\sin(nx)\,dx + \int_{0}^{\pi}k\sin(nx)\,dx \right].$ Since the two integrals are equal, $b_n = \dfrac{2k}{\pi} \int_{0}^{\pi}\sin(nx)\,dx.$ Now, $\int_{0}^{\pi}\sin(nx)\,dx = \dfrac{1-(-1)^n}{n}.$ Hence, $b_n = \dfrac{2k}{n\pi} \left(1-(-1)^n\right).$ For odd harmonics, $(-1)^n=-1,$ therefore, $b_n=\dfrac{4k}{n\pi}.$ Step 3: Third harmonic For $n=3,$ $a_3=0,$ and $b_3=\dfrac{4k}{3\pi}.$ The question states that the sum of the third-harmonic cosine and sine coefficients is $a_3+b_3=\dfrac{2}{3\pi}.$ Since $a_3=0,$ $\dfrac{4k}{3\pi} = \dfrac{2}{3\pi}.$ Therefore, $4k=2$ $k=\dfrac{1}{2}.$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ee:2026:q30.question: The operating characteristic of a reactance relay is given by $X \leq 1\ \Omega$, where $X$ is the reactance calculated by the relay. detailed_solution.concept: Power Systems - Switch Gear and Protection
detailed_solution.markdown:
The operating characteristic of the reactance relay is

$X \leq 1~\Omega$

where $X$ is the reactance seen by the relay.

The impedance seen by the relay is

$Z=R+jX$

The corresponding admittance is

$Y=\dfrac{1}{Z}=G+jB$

where

$G=\dfrac{R}{R^2+X^2},

\qquad

B=-\dfrac{X}{R^2+X^2}$

Since

$R=\dfrac{G}{G^2+B^2},

\qquad

X=-\dfrac{B}{G^2+B^2}$

substitute into the relay characteristic

$X\le 1$

to obtain

$-\dfrac{B}{G^2+B^2}\le 1$

Rearranging,

$G^2+B^2+B\ge 0$

Completing the square,

$G^2+\left(B+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2\ge\dfrac14$

Multiplying both sides by 4,

$4G^2+4\left(B+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2\ge 1$

or

$4G^2+(2B+1)^2\ge 1$

Hence,

$G^2+\left(B+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2\ge\dfrac{1}{4}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

$\vec{B}_2 = -\dfrac{n}{\sqrt{2}}\cos(2\omega t + \pi/4)(0\hat{x} + 1\hat{y} + 1\hat{z})$

What is the expression for the induced rms voltage in loop A?

ee:2026:q42.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 42
ee:2026:q42.question:
A system is characterized by the following state equation and output equation ($u$: input, $\mathbf{x}$: state vector, $y$: output):

What are the values of $a$ and $b$ for which the poles of the transfer function are at $-2+j3$ and $-2-j3$?

Characteristic polynomial of $$A = \begin{bmatrix}a&b\\-a&0\end{bmatrix}$$:

$\det(\lambda I - A) = \lambda(\lambda - a) + ab = \lambda^2 - a\lambda + ab$

Desired poles at $-2 \pm j3$ -> desired characteristic polynomial:

$(\lambda+2-j3)(\lambda+2+j3) = \lambda^2 + 4\lambda + 13$

Matching coefficients:

$-a = 4 \Rightarrow a = -4$

$ab = 13 \Rightarrow b = \dfrac{13}{-4} = -3.25$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ee:2026:q53.title: GATE EE 2026 | Set 1 | Question: 53

Consider a linear arrangement of seven bulbs, each of which can be in the ON or OFF states. The initial configuration of the bulbs is shown in the figure. In every Step, the states of the bulbs are changed based on the following rules:

Any OFF bulb with exactly one ON neighbor at the end of the previous Step is turned ON.
Any ON bulb with both neighbors ON at the end of the previous Step is turned OFF.
The state of any bulb not meeting the conditions above is left unchanged.

Initial: ON ON ON OFF ON ON ON
Step 1: ON ON OFF OFF OFF ON ON
Step 2: ON OFF OFF ON OFF OFF ON

The number of bulbs which are ON at the end of Step 8 is ______

detailed_solution.markdown:
Step-by-step Transition:

Step 1:

For bulb 3 (OFF), it has one ON neighbor (bulb 2). It turns ON.

For bulb 5 (ON), both neighbors (bulbs 4 and 6) are ON. It turns OFF.

New configuration after Step 1: [1,1,1,0,0,1,1]

Step 2:

For bulb 4 (OFF), it has exactly one ON neighbor (bulb 5 was OFF). It turns ON.

For bulb 6 (ON), both neighbors (bulbs 5 and 7) are OFF. So, it remains ON.

New configuration after Step 2: [1,1,1,1,0,1,1]

Continuing similarly, we perform this process up to Step 8, applying the rules repeatedly: [1,1,1,1,0,1,1] -> [1,1,1,0,1,1,1] -> [1,1,0,1,1,0,1] ... and so on.

Finally, after Step 8, the bulb configuration is determined to be: [0,1,1,0,1,0,1]

Counting the number of ON bulbs at Step 8 gives us 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

$P$ and $Q$ are two positive integers such that $P^{2} = Q^{2} + 13$.

The product of the numbers $P$ and $Q$ is _________

detailed_solution.markdown:
$P^{2} - Q^{2} = 13$

$\Rightarrow (P-Q)(P+Q) = 13$

Since 13 is prime and $P, Q$ are positive integers:

$P - Q = 1$ and $P + Q = 13$

Solving: $P = 7,\ Q = 6$

Product $= 7 \times 6 = 42$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.
